text:
sam: Seeing a surge of GPU attach failures in ap-southeast1. Provisioning stuck in PENDING for ~2m and then times out. Suspect local NVMe IOPS saturation from cleanup jobs. Anyone oncall?

aj: looking at metrics now — iowait + disk write latency spiked around 02:14 UTC. Attach logs: `attach_id=gp-9a3f` shows `io timeout` during image cleanup.

aj: quick screenshot of grafana query: /d/infra/gpu-provisioning?orgId=1&var-region=ap-southeast1 (linked)

maria: ugh, this again. Last week we saw similar but it was scrub overlap. Is janitor concurrency still at 32 for that region?

aj: yes, currently region.ap-southeast1.janitor.max_concurrency=32 per config.

linh: FYI kernel roll from yesterday (5.16) increased fsync throughput for overlay -> more synchronous writes during delete. Might surface as higher write bursts during cleanup.

sam: do we have iostat from an affected host?

aj: grabbed one from node gnode-aps1-042:
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await  r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         12.00  340.00  120.00 20480.00   60.42    8.13  24.1   4.1    26.0   0.72  87.6
```
Shows sustained write pressure, avgqu-sz high.

devops: confirmed. The cleanup worker blasts deletes concurrently which expands write amplification for overlayfs layers. Combined with current batch workloads that's exceeding the drive's IOPS profile.

maria: temporary mitigation: lower janitor concurrency to 6 for ap-southeast1 and enable delete-throttle feature (rate-limit deletes to 200MB/s). That should drop the queue and allow provisioning to proceed.

linh: i'd also like to roll back the kernel patch on a small canary fleet if we can. The timing may align with our maintenance window in 90m.

sam: agree on both. For immediate relief i'll flip concurrency and throttle. @aj can you run the config change and confirm?

aj: doing now. command:
```
rbctl set-config region.ap-southeast1.janitor.max_concurrency=6
rbctl set-config region.ap-southeast1.janitor.delete_rate_limit=200MB/s
```
Applying... ✅

aj: rechecked node — iowait and avgqu-sz dropped within ~30s on the canary nodes. Attach queue cleared and GPU attaches started succeeding again.

oncall-bot: alert suppressed: GPU_PROVISIONING_FAILURES ap-southeast1 -> notified 6 users.

maria: great. Next steps: create a short-lived rollout to keep concurrency lower until kernel rollback or we ship a janitor change that does exponential backoff on deletes. I'll open a ticket and a follow-up PR.

devops: note on cost: throttling deletes prolongs reclaim window which raises ephemeral capacity footprint ~10% — might bump Dedicated cost if sustained. We should track reclaimed bytes and decide whether to allow slight capacity drift or accelerate kernel rollback.

linh: i'll schedule kernel rollback canary for ap-southeast1 in the 90m window. If rollback reduces fsync pressure we can revert the throttle.

sam: filing triage ticket and assigning owners. PR (draft) from aj: https://git.internal/r/redwood/janitor/pulls/482 (will add backoff logic + metrics).

aj: PR will add `--delete-backoff-ms` and a `--max-inflight-deletes` flag. Planning smoke test on canaries.

maria: also add a dashboard row for `janitor.inflight_deletes` and `delete_rate_bytes` so we can alarm earlier.

sam: perfect. I'll keep monitoring and will post updates. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

aj: follow-up in #eng-sre after rollback results.

linh: if anything regresses ping me directly.

sam: closing this thread once rollback verified.
